links.comparator_used: Co-designed PreA (GPT-4o mini with prompting and agent techniques, no additional fine-tuning) versus the same model further fine-tuned on local primary care dialogues
links.outcome: Expert-rated quality of referral reports (history-taking, diagnosis, test ordering) in a simulation with 300 virtual patient profiles
links.effect: Co-designed (not fine-tuned) vs local data-tuned: history-taking 4.56 ± 0.65 vs 3.86 ± 0.81; diagnosis 4.67 ± 0.55 vs 2.47 ± 1.44; test ordering 4.23 ± 1.09 vs 2.21 ± 1.12; all P < 0.001
links.tradeoff: The fine-tuned model replicated real-world primary care deficiencies. It omitted guideline-recommended history elements and demographics, failed to give diagnoses in 30.0% (90/300) and to suggest tests in 39.3% (118/300) of cases when needed, and mimicked an unfriendly clinician tone.
links.quote: The co-designed model achieved significantly higher-quality rating scores than the data-tuned counterpart (the co-designed model further fine-tuned on the primary care dialogues) group across all domains: history-taking (without data-tuned 4.56 ± 0.65 versus data-tuned 3.86 ± 0.81; P < 0.001; Fig. 4b ), diagnosis (without data-tuned 4.67 ± 0.55 versus data-tuned 2.47 ± 1.44; P < 0.001) and testing order (without data-tuned 4.23 ± 1.09 versus data-tuned 2.21 ± 1.12; P < 0.001).
